desc:
Drupal SEO and page speed optimization makes content heavy sites faster and easier for search engines to read. Ecom Swift LLC tunes caching, images and markup, sets up titles, sitemaps and structured data, and reports what changed.

## Why do speed and search setup matter for Drupal sites?

Speed and search setup matter because they decide whether people can reach your content and whether search engines can understand it. Drupal is powerful for large content libraries, but a site with many content types, views and modules can grow slow and untidy over time. Slow pages frustrate visitors, and unclear titles, duplicate addresses and missing structured data make it harder for search engines to read the site.

Drupal gives you the tools to fix this. The work is to configure them well and keep them tuned as the site grows.

## What slows a content heavy site

The usual causes are plain. Caching is off or set too cautiously, so every visit rebuilds the page. Images are uploaded at camera size and displayed small. CSS and JavaScript load as many separate files. Views and database queries pull far more data than the page shows. Old modules add scripts nobody uses.

Search problems are just as common. Many pages share the same title pattern, canonical addresses are missing, redirects chain through several steps, and headings are used for styling rather than structure. Each of these is fixable without rewriting your content.

## How these fixes affect results

Faster pages let visitors read, click and enquire without waiting, and that matters most on mobile connections. Cleaner markup and correct headings help search engines understand what each page is about. Canonical addresses and redirect fixes prevent the same content from competing with itself. Structured data for articles gives search engines labeled facts, such as headline, author and date.

We cannot say where a page will rank or how much traffic it will earn. Search results depend on your content, your competitors and many other signals. What we deliver is a technically clean, measured site that gives your content a fair chance.

## What a good Drupal speed and search setup includes

- A speed test of important pages before any change, so you can compare afterward.
- Page and block caching configured for your editors' workflow.
- Images resized, served in suitable dimensions and lazy loaded.
- CSS and JavaScript aggregation tuned.
- The Metatag and XML sitemap modules configured with sensible defaults.
- Title and description patterns for each content type.
- Canonical addresses and redirect clean up.
- Structured data for articles and similar content.
- Template markup tidied so headings follow a logical order.
- Database and view query tuning, plus duplicate content fixes, in larger packages.

## What we do

We measure first, using a sample of your most important pages. We then change settings and templates on a staging copy, starting with caching and images because they usually help most. Next we configure the search modules, write the title and description patterns and fix address problems.

The Basic package covers caching, images and search basics for a few key pages. Standard adds deeper speed work, patterns for each content type and structured data. Premium adds query tuning, duplicate content fixes, template cleanup and a keyword plan for chosen pages. We retest after the changes and give you a before and after comparison with a list of everything we touched.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us which pages matter most for visitors and for search.
- Upload images at a sensible size from now on.
- Clear caches after major edits, or let us set automatic clearing.
- Keep page titles unique and descriptive.
- Recheck speed after adding new modules.

**Avoid:**
- Installing several optimization modules that overlap.
- Disabling caching to see edits faster, instead of fixing cache rules.
- Stuffing keywords into titles and headings.
- Changing page addresses without redirects.
- Treating speed as a one-time job.

## Who this is for

This suits a publisher or association with hundreds of articles and a site that feels heavy. It suits a company whose pages share the same title pattern and never appear well in search, and a team preparing a site for a campaign that will bring extra visitors.

## What we need from you

Send your site address and the pages you care about most. Tell us whether Google Search Console or analytics already exist. We work as a developer user on your site and never ask for passwords. A staging copy is ideal, and we can help create one. We reply with a short plan before any change.
